## 2. Unit structure

### U1 — Foundations & Strategy · L01, L02, L03, L04

Why projects fail; strategic alignment; project, program, portfolio; PMBOK 7 principles and performance domains; roles and the PM profession.

### U2 — Life Cycles & Initiating · L05, L06, L07, L08

Predictive, agile, hybrid life cycles; charter and stakeholder analysis; agile role system; tailoring for software and data projects.

### U3 — Planning the Work · L09, L10, L11, L12, L13, L14

Scope and WBS; estimation; CPM/PERT scheduling; cost, budget, quality, and data-quality planning.

### U4 — Risk, Uncertainty & Control · L15, L16, L17, L18, L19, L20

Risk management aligned to ISO 31000; PERT and simulation; procurement; EVM and adaptive monitoring; change control.

### U5 — Adaptive Delivery & Teams · L21, L22, L23, L24, L25, L26

Scrum, Kanban, SAFe overview, hybrid; team performance; stakeholder communication and negotiation; data-specific team topologies.

### U6 — Integration, Ethics & Closing · L27, L28, L29, L30

Master planning; ethics and professional responsibility (PMI Code); sustainability; closure, lessons learned, benefits realization.

### U7 — Synthesis & Capstone · L31, L32

AI-assisted project management; capstone defense and course synthesis.

## 3. Course learning outcomes — teaching & assessment chain

### CLO1 — Understand

Given a PMBOK 7 performance-domain map, define and correctly classify the twelve principles, the eight performance domains, and predictive, adaptive, and hybrid life-cycle models; given a project vignette, justify a life-cycle choice using at least three explicit criteria (requirements volatility, regulatory exposure, feedback cadence, team distribution).

*Taught in:* L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L08. *Assessed by:* Midterm, quizzes.

### CLO2 — Apply

Given a project brief, construct a deliverable-oriented WBS that passes the 100% rule, derive three-point (PERT) estimates for its work packages, build a CPM network with correctly computed float, and produce a levelled, time-feasible Gantt baseline within a fixed window.

*Taught in:* L06, L09, L10, L11, L12. *Assessed by:* Assignment 1, Labs 1-4, Midterm.

### CLO3 — Apply

Given activity cost data, develop a bottom-up budget with S-curve and a quality/data-quality plan containing at least four measurable metrics and eight enforceable data-quality rules; given PV, EV, and AC, compute the full earned-value set (CV, SV, CPI, SPI, EAC variants, TCPI) correctly.

*Taught in:* L13, L14, L18. *Assessed by:* Midterm (primary); practiced via CS-17, CS-26, CS-57, CS-62 and capstone budget.

### CLO4 — Analyze/Evaluate

Given a project scenario, identify at least eighteen distinct risks as normalized cause-risk-effect statements, quantify at least one risk via EMV or Monte Carlo simulation, and propose responses with named owners, triggers, and residual risk; given PV/EV/AC data, diagnose project health and recommend a justified recovery action.

*Taught in:* L15, L16, L17, L18, L19, L20. *Assessed by:* Assignment 3, Labs 7-8, Midterm, Capstone checkpoint.

### CLO5 — Apply

Given a delivery context, operate Scrum, Kanban, and hybrid flow systems: produce a sprint plan with a single-sentence goal and capacity check, set WIP limits justified by flow metrics, rewrite a feature-first backlog into a hypothesis-driven one for a data/ML project, and prepare a working agreement plus a BATNA-based negotiation plan for a sponsor conflict.

*Taught in:* L05, L07, L08, L21, L22, L23, L24, L25, L26. *Assessed by:* Assignment 4, Labs 9-12, Case portfolio, Capstone.

### CLO6 — Create

Given a project brief, design a complete, internally consistent project management plan (scope, schedule, and cost baselines plus risk, communication, quality, and data-governance plans), then defend its trade-offs — tailoring cuts, risk investments, ethics and AI-use positions — in a rubric-scored oral defense with follow-up questions.

*Taught in:* L27, L28, L29, L30, L31, L32. *Assessed by:* Capstone, Final exam, Case portfolio.
